substeps.caption: From an operator's eyes at the opening, looking up under the header: the bay has a roof, and two stream cameras hang from it on short drops, one at the back looking forward, one behind the header looking back. Each is a Pi 5 with an HQ Camera and a Camera Module 3 Wide on a pan-tilt head.

What each Wide covers, 102 x 67 degrees: the back one (blue) 94 % of the tray's floor and the arm coming in, the front one (orange) 82 %, the instruments' fronts where the arm works. The top of the back one's picture looks out into the room, so its stream gets a privacy mask there; the front one sees none of it.

What the back unit's Wide sees: nearly the whole presented tray from behind, 94 % of its floor, and the arm reaching in. Rendered from the camera's own position and aim, 102 degrees across (Raspberry Pi's figures: 102 x 67, 120 diagonal).

Now the front unit's Wide, from behind the header.

What the front unit's Wide sees, looking back: the instruments' fronts and the gripper standing the vial on the doser's shuttle fork, outside the port in its panel; 82 % of the tray's floor and none of the room. The wrist's own camera (a RealSense D405) sees the last few centimetres.
